features.name: argument_has_first_person_singular
features.definition: Does the original argument text contain at least one explicit first-person singular pronoun (I, me, my, mine, myself)?
features.spec: Read only df['argument']. If missing/non-string return null; empty string gives 0. Normalise curly apostrophes to ' then: df['argument'].apply(lambda s: None if not isinstance(s,str) else int(bool(re.search(r"\b(?:i|me|my|mine|myself)\b|\bi'(?:m|ve|d|ll)\b", s.replace('’',"'"), flags=re.I)))). Counts any occurrence anywhere in the argument, including within quotations (raw mechanical match, no semantic filtering). Title and comments are not read.

h0: argument_has_first_person_singular has no association with the probability of view change (delta).
h1: Discussions with argument_has_first_person_singular = 1 have a higher probability of view change than those with 0.
note: Binary presence per the hypothesis (no count/share). Pronoun list (I, me, my, mine, myself, and I-contractions) is an operational assumption; case-insensitive so lowercase informal 'i' counts, and quotations are not excluded. Argument is current text and may include edits or outcome announcements (raw text not outcome-free or pre-outcome). OLS on binary delta is a linear probability model; association only, not causal.
